clue.text: After which the participants come out of their shells

definitions.text: After which the participants come out of their shells

parts.words: After which the participants come out of their shells
parts.note: reads like hatching chicks, but the shells are the light racing boats rowers sit in, and the crews climb out after the event

explanation.surface: Something after which creatures emerge from their shells, like a hatching.
explanation.walkthrough: A rowing shell is a narrow racing boat; the clue paints eggs hatching.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowers in a regatta sit in shells and climb out of them once the contest is over.

definitions.meaning: to avoid someone is to keep away from them deliberately
the clipped drill-sergeant's command for standing to attention

explanation.surface: Ignore anyone seeking the limelight.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep away from is a synonym, and the clipped parade-ground order for 'Attention!' has the same spelling.

indicators.note: the girl's letters sit out, around the other word, holding it

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
to lob is to throw in a high arc

explanation.surface: An all-embracing reason for ejecting a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worldwide in scope is all-embracing, a synonym of comprehensive.

definitions.meaning: from the idiom 'swear like a ...', the proverbial heavy curser
a cavalryman or private in an armoured or mounted unit

explanation.surface: A man who curses, being in the army.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'swear like a trooper' makes the cavalry private the archetypal curser.

parts.note: seems to describe a lost pet searching, but means a dog that does the looking on behalf of its blind owner

explanation.surface: A lost pet searching for the person it belongs to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looking for' means seeing on someone's behalf, not searching.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog trained to lead a blind person does the seeing for its owner.

clue.text: Enthronement of firm king has appeal to the country

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
R is the abbreviation for rex, king
O is the exclamation of invocation, as in 'O Lord'
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A monarch's crowning gives the business-minded king popularity across the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowning a monarch is the ceremony of enthronement, the two being near synonyms.

clue.text: Intended taking one quarter out of capital

indicators.note: the quarter is taken out of the word for capital, leaving the rest

parts.note: finance is capital, money for investment
N, north, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone intending to take a quarter of the money for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intended' is a noun here: the person one is engaged to.
explanation.definitionFit: One's intended is the person one is engaged to marry, a betrothed man.

clue.text: Sportsman doesn't quite make the North Pole, losing direction

indicators.note: the letters fail to make the polar words and instead form something else, a rearrangement
the compass point is lost from the polar name

parts.note: N, north, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: An explorer falls short of the North Pole, having lost his bearings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing direction' drops one N from NORTHPOLE, leaving ORTHPOLE to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A caver who explores underground shafts as a sport is a sportsman of a sort.

clue.text: More work here — or less, many hope!

definitions.text: More work here — or less, many hope!

parts.words: More work here — or less, many hope!
parts.note: Thomas More's work is the book about an ideal state, where people hope to toil less

explanation.surface: A remark about longer or shorter working hours.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Thomas More wrote a book naming an ideal commonwealth; 'More work' is that book.
explanation.definitionFit: The imaginary perfect society of Thomas More's book is where people dream of working less.

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A school for horses that compete in point-to-point races.
explanation.walkthrough: A point-to-point is a British amateur steeplechase; here it is read as one compass point, then 'to', then another.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous English boarding school is an establishment for educating boys.

parts.note: the vampire is a nobleman with a title, and his diet is blood

explanation.surface: A single-word question naming the famous vampire.
explanation.walkthrough: Dracula is a count obsessed with blood; the answer is also a medical test.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical test of blood cells doubles as a description of the vampire nobleman.

indicators.note: the doctor goes into the prison word

parts.note: gaol is the British spelling of jail
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor going into jail to search a prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frisk' suggests a body search but is the verb to leap about playfully.
explanation.definitionFit: To frisk is to skip about playfully, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Protection on landing for party setting up American commerce

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means written upwards, so this word is turned backwards

parts.note: Lab is short for the Labour Party
US is short for American, United States
trade is commerce

explanation.surface: Safety measures for an airport arrival, for a political group promoting US business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landing' suggests aircraft but is the top of a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: A row of posts with a rail guards the edge of a stair landing against falls.

clue.text: Blank sheet to finish a learned discourse

parts.note: end is a finish
a paper is a learned essay delivered or published

explanation.surface: A clean page on which to complete an academic essay.
explanation.definitionFit: The blank leaf pasted inside a book's cover is a sheet with nothing printed on it.

parts.note: not a written message but a person who lets property, in American usage

explanation.surface: A piece of correspondence mailed from the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: Letter From America was a long-running BBC radio talk by Alistair Cooke; here a letter is one who lets.
explanation.definitionFit: An American estate agent arranges lettings, so is a 'letter' of property.

definitions.meaning: the British Sunday newspaper of that name

explanation.surface: The Spectator, a magazine published every week.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spectator is itself a British weekly, which leads the eye away.
explanation.definitionFit: A watcher is a synonym of spectator, and a long-running British Sunday paper carries the name.

clue.text: Profit in a way in opposition

indicators.note: the profit word sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
gain is profit

explanation.surface: Making money in a manner that goes against the grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Being opposed to something is being in opposition to it, the same meaning.

clue.text: Song composed about the present time

indicators.note: the calm word goes about the era abbreviation, around it

parts.note: serene means calm and composed
AD, anno Domini, names the present era

explanation.surface: A song written about our own age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' looks like the act of writing music but means calm.
explanation.definitionFit: A love song sung beneath a window at night is a kind of song.

clue.text: Muse involved with Art for ages

indicators.note: the two words become entangled together and rearranged

explanation.surface: A source of inspiration engaged with painting for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ages' is a verb here: grows older.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that ages grows older and ripens, a synonym in verb form.

parts.note: Man is the Isle of Man, and its surroundings on the map are the waters about it

explanation.surface: A remark on humankind's surroundings from a geographer's view.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man lies in the stretch of sea between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is surrounded by this body of water between Great Britain and Ireland.

clue.text: He's involved in new rate of afterburning

indicators.note: the pronoun is caught up inside the other letters
the letters of rate are made new, rearranged

parts.note: he is, simply the word he

explanation.surface: A man engaged in a new rate of combustion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's' reads as the subject of the sentence but simply supplies two letters; 'new' makes REAT, which 'involved in' wraps round them. Afterburning is jet-engine jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: In jet engines, afterburning is also called reheat: extra fuel burnt in the exhaust for thrust.

parts.note: sent is slang for transported with delight

explanation.surface: A railway guard thrilled with his job.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier posted to keep watch is a guard.

indicators.note: the wool word goes in the school abbreviation

parts.note: ket is a Scots word for a matted fleece

explanation.surface: Making a picture of tangled wool at school.
explanation.definitionFit: To sketch is to draw roughly, a synonym.

parts.note: a chart is a plan or map
to reuse is to recycle

explanation.surface: An environmental scheme for recycling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' suggests ecology but is a colour, named after the liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellowish-green shade takes its name from the French herbal liqueur of that colour.

definitions.meaning: capital as an exclamation means excellent
a money penalty imposed for an offence

explanation.surface: The death penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Excellent is an old sense of capital, and a money penalty is a punishment.

indicators.note: the rider comes after the office letters

parts.note: a PS, postscript, is a rider added to a letter

explanation.surface: A horseman trailing behind snobbish diplomats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' suggests a horseman but is an addition to a document.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffs are dandified upper-class men, close to vain dandies.

definitions.meaning: to manage something is to deal with it
a slang word for a name or title

explanation.surface: Contriving to earn a title.
explanation.definitionFit: To deal with something is to manage it, and a slang word for a name or title is the same word.

clue.text: Prank ceased being funny when father came in

indicators.note: the father word comes into the jumbled letters
the letters of ceased behave oddly, rearranged

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: The joke stopped being amusing once Dad arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a joke going stale; 'being funny' gives ESCADE, and 'came in' lets father enter its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischievous adventure or prank is a synonym.
